brief.title: amcheck: add gist_index_check() to verify GiST indexes
brief.problem: amcheck can verify B-tree and GIN indexes but has no check for GiST, so users cannot detect GiST index corruption with it. Message #1 does not say more about who needs it; it presents the patch as the next step after GIN support in PG19.
brief.proposed_design: A new amcheck function walks the GiST index depth-first and checks that each downlink tuple fits inside its parent key, and that the tree is balanced. On a mismatch it locks parent and child in page-split order and rechecks, so concurrent splits do not give false reports. With heapallindexed it also checks that heap tuples are in the index, using tuple normalization moved from the B-tree checker into shared code.
user_visible_surface: New SQL function gist_index_check(index regclass, heapallindexed boolean) returns void in amcheck.
amcheck extension version 1.6, with upgrade script amcheck--1.5--1.6.sql.
New corruption error messages, for example deleted internal page, deleted page with tuples, internal page became leaf.
Early patch versions add GiST and GIN checks to pg_amcheck; later versions in the thread no longer include that part.
author_claims: The GiST function is in decent shape and was only rebased from earlier work.
Rechecking with parent and child locks makes the check safe while concurrent inserts split pages.
A tester reported run times of about 0.3s to 14s on 10M-row indexes across 9 core opclasses, and found no problems.
Version 0003 cuts memory for heapallindexed on 2M rows from about 300MB to about 1MB.
Version 0003 reports a link of InvalidBlockNumber and a root page marked as split as corruption, where the check used to extend the index or crash.
brief.thread_state: Several reviewers sent fixes and the CommitFest entry is Ready for Committer, but it has moved through 7 CommitFests. The latest message (2026-09-25) adds new review fixes in 0003 and asks if a committer will pick it up, and no committer has replied.
unclear: Whether the pg_amcheck patches are dropped, deferred to another thread, or still planned.
Whether anyone has reviewed the new 0003 fixes and the TAP test that corrupts the index file.
Whether the check is safe and correct for GiST opclasses without a compress function, beyond the reproducers in the thread.
Which lock level gist_index_check takes on the index and the table, and whether it blocks writes.
Whether the downlink block-number checks raised in message #3 are now fully handled by 0003.

objections.title: Lock strength and page-deletion concerns from the 2019 attempt are unanswered
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA runs gist_index_check on a busy production table while VACUUM deletes empty GiST leaf pages. The check follows a downlink to a deleted or reused page, or re-finds the wrong parent, and reports corruption that is not there. The DBA then rebuilds a healthy index or opens a false bug report.
objections.argument: [P3] is the same function by the same author, returned in 2019. The recorded concern there was the heavyweight lock level (AccessShareLock against an earlier ShareLock), whether the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() holds here, and concurrent page deletion. None of the 17 messages states the lock level or explains why the re-check is safe against page deletion. Message #4 touches concurrency only for downlink bounds, and the commit message only says that locks follow page-split order. [P5] shows that holding several buffer locks at once was also asked to carry a strong justification.
objections.author_must_show: Which heavyweight lock does gist_index_check take, and why is the parent and child re-check correct under that lock when VACUUM deletes GiST pages concurrently?

critic.reasoning: The visible thread and patch prose do not state the relation lock level or address concurrent page deletion, the two points recorded in [P3]. [P5] concerns a B-tree metapage check and gives only weak support.

refuted.title: Concurrency recheck relies on GiST split and deletion internals, never confirmed
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release changes how GiST splits or recycles deleted pages, and verify_gist.c is not updated to match. A DBA then runs gist_index_check on a busy index, gets a corruption error that is false, and reindexes or files a bug. Nothing in the build or the tests fails when the two drift apart.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the recheck takes parent and child locks "in the same order as page split does", so verify_gist.c copies assumptions from the GiST split and deletion code. In the earlier attempt [P3], a reviewer doubted that the parent re-find logic carried over from gistfinishsplit() applies here, asked how concurrent page deletion affects it, and questioned the heavyweight lock strength. The visible thread does not answer these points or say which lock the function takes. No committer who knows GiST has engaged here, so whoever commits it would own this coupling.
refuted.author_must_show: Which relation lock does gist_index_check take, and why does the parent re-find stay correct under concurrent page deletion as well as concurrent splits?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which asks the same lock-level and page-deletion questions. The remaining point, that a verifier can drift from the access method code, applies equally to the existing B-tree and GIN checkers in amcheck.

refuted.title: pg_amcheck integration dropped without a stated plan
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs pg_amcheck nightly across all databases and assumes every index is covered. GiST indexes are skipped without notice, so corruption in them goes undetected until queries return wrong results.
refuted.argument: Message #1 and message #2 shipped pg_amcheck support for GiST and GIN, and message #3 suggested keeping it apart from BRIN. The later series contains only the SQL function, and the thread never says whether the pg_amcheck part is dropped, deferred, or moved to another thread. So pg_amcheck users get no benefit from the new function.
refuted.author_must_show: Will GiST checking reach pg_amcheck in this series or in a named follow-up, and what does pg_amcheck report for GiST indexes until then?

critic.reasoning: pg_amcheck skips GiST indexes today, so the patch does not create or worsen the scenario. Message #1 shows GIN checking shipped in amcheck without pg_amcheck support, so a function-only step follows existing practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch appears to need some work and has not been updated in several
weeks, so marking Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pageinspect - add functions on GIN and GiST indexes from gevel
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Tomas Vondra, Ashutosh Sharma, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the gevel module's functions for GiST, SP-GiST and GIN indexes into pageinspect, with tests and docs. The functions show whole-index statistics, print the tree and its stored objects, and estimate GIN value counts and query matches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the functions read the whole index, while pageinspect inspects single pages, so the code belongs in a new extension or should be rewritten as page-level functions. Peter Eisentraut also found that the patch no longer compiled and that the stats functions returned one formatted text value where they should return a row with columns. The author planned a new contrib module but posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after three weeks of waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The proposed patch uses a very different approach, reading the whole index,
not individual pages. Why should it be part of pageinspect?

precedents_retrieved.title: amcheck verification for GiST
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST verification function to contrib/amcheck that checks parent/child key consistency and that all leaf pages are at the same depth. Later versions hold buffer locks on parent and child pages together and take only an AccessShareLock on the relation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan questioned whether the checks are safe under an AccessShareLock, since Heikki's v6 had used a ShareLock. He doubted that the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() applies here and asked how concurrent page deletion could affect it. Andrey Borodin did not answer these questions for about two months, so Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My main concern now is the heavyweight lock strength needed by the new function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel CREATE INDEX for GiST indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel CREATE INDEX for GiST, limited to unsorted builds without buffering, with workers inserting tuples into a shared index. Page splits are detected through fake LSNs from GetFakeLSNForUnloggedRel(), and the pages are WAL-logged at the end.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the code: Andrey Borodin found it correct and suggested only a refactor of the LSN choice. In the last message the author said he was worried that GiST would have too many build methods, because a parallel build can use much more CPU without being faster. He said parallel buffered builds might settle this, but he had no time to study them and someone else would have to. The visible messages show no further work and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But for parallel builds it's not that clear - it can easily happen that we use much more CPU, without speeding anything up.

precedents_retrieved.title: Verify true root on replicas with amcheck
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the regular bt_check_index() function in amcheck verify the true root of a B-Tree index, so the check also works on replicas. It does this by locking the metapage and the potential root page at the same time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Peter Geoghegan asked what true root corruption meant and what symptom it caused, and he did not want to commit a patch that holds multiple buffer locks without a strong justification. The patch also stopped applying, and David Steele returned it after no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Your patch looks like it gets it right (it won't deadlock with other
sessions that access the metapage), but I hesitate to commit it
without a strong justification.

precedents_retrieved.title: Speeding up GIST index builds using popcount
precedents_retrieved.summary: Patch 0001 makes hemdistsign() in tsgistidx.c and similar GiST code XOR the signature bitvectors in 64-bit chunks and count bits with popcount64, which speeds up GiST index builds on tsvector by about 12-50% depending on siglen. Patch 0002 removes the pg_popcount32/64 function pointer on non-x86 platforms so that calls go directly to __builtin_popcount.
precedents_retrieved.objection: John Naylor declined to pass 0002 to a committer because of its code complexity, and said full asm popcount support on Arm would be the better approach. For 0001, he asked the author to measure whether the earlier 1-7% regression at small default siglen still exists before applying it in all contrib modules, and the pointer alignment question was still being worked on. The author's last message (August 2021) promised replies to the other review comments, and no revised patch appears before the entry was returned in October.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Readability counts, and as it stands I don't feel comfortable asking a committer to read 0002.

precedents_retrieved.title: support for box type in SP-GiST index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds an SP-GiST operator class for the box type that treats a 2D box as a point in 4D space and indexes it with a quad-tree analogue (q4d) splitting each node into 16 regions. It also adds a traversalValue field to SP-GiST so inner_consistent can carry computed bounds to child nodes, and switches range_spgist.c from reconstructValue to it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for performance numbers, a fuller explanation of the patch's purpose, and a rebase, and the patch was set to Waiting on Author. The author did not reply, so it was closed after about three months without a response.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I closed this patch as "returned with feedback" because the author
didn't reply in three months.

precedents_retrieved.title: Better tracking of free space during SP-GiST index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that SP-GiST index build track several recently used pages per page category instead of only the last one, so that free space is reused better. A fixed table gives more cache slots to leaf pages than to other categories.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the patch, and Tomas Vondra called it a solid improvement. After review, Tom Lane planned to make page selection by free space more efficient. He did not have time for that before the commitfest ended, so he asked for the entry to be marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I doubt I will get to it this week, so let's mark it RWF for this fest.

roaster_notes.note: One objection only. The precedent reason that may still apply is the lock-safety question from [P3]. Message #1 links the earlier thread but does not summarize how that question ended.

The user-facing contract follows existing amcheck practice. gist_index_check(index regclass, heapallindexed boolean) matches the naming and argument style of bt_index_check and gin_index_check, and it comes with a normal 1.5 to 1.6 upgrade script. The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump state, and it does not change behaviour for existing users. Two points could not be checked from the material. First, the documentation hunk shown does not state the lock level, while the bt_index_check entry does; this is a docs gap that belongs to the locking question covered by another angle. Second, pg_amcheck does not support GIN either, so the dropped pg_amcheck part is an existing gap and not a new departure from practice.

The proposal adds a read-only contrib function and an amcheck 1.5 to 1.6 upgrade script, with no change to on-disk format, WAL, protocol or core catalogs. Not checkable without code: whether the parent-child recheck is safe on a hot standby during GiST redo, and whether 0003 stops every path that could extend the index.

The material shows no new privilege or exposure path: gist_index_check is a read-only amcheck function, and amcheck normally revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC. Without the code I could not check whether amcheck--1.5--1.6.sql does that, which lock level the function takes, or whether the 0003 crash fixes (P_NEW extension, NULL root) were reviewed.
The function lives in contrib/amcheck and adds no cost for users who do not call it. It follows the existing B-tree and GIN checkers, so fit and hot-path cost are not concerns.

Postgres has no existing way to verify a GiST index. amcheck covers B-tree, GIN and heap, pageinspect only dumps raw GiST pages for manual reading, and REINDEX replaces the index without reporting corruption. I know of no extension that does this check, and the proposal extends amcheck instead of adding a second mechanism.

No demand objection. amcheck already checks B-tree and GIN, so a GiST check fills a gap in an existing tool. GiST backs core opclasses, exclusion constraints and contrib modules, and several independent reviewers and testers worked on the patch over many CommitFests (messages #3, #6, #8, #12, #16, #17). The cost is a contrib function that runs only when called, so it falls on its users and touches no hot path. The thread cites no field reports of GiST corruption, but a committer would likely accept parity with the existing checkers as enough reason.
